title: Solving Two-Step Linear Equations
subject: Mathematics
text: A two-step linear equation takes the general form ax + b = c, where a and b are known coefficients and x is the unknown variable. Solving two-step equations requires isolating the variable term by applying inverse operations in the reverse order of arithmetic operations. Step 1: Use addition or subtraction to eliminate the constant term b from the side containing the variable (e.g., subtract b from both sides). Step 2: Use multiplication or division to eliminate coefficient a (e.g., divide both sides by a). When equations contain parentheses, such as a(x + b) = c, expand the expression using the distributive property first, or divide both sides by a if divisible without remainder.
